## Council question

How does Truthtrance interact with an existing binding deal?

## Why this needs a ruling

The v0.8 clarification says to consider possible answers ignoring binding deals, then includes binding deals among commitments assumed fulfilled. It also says Truthtrance wins a conflict while prohibiting an answer that makes an existing deal impossible.

## Answer needed

Give one consistent precedence rule. Example: a player has promised not to attack a territory and is then asked a question whose truthful answer would commit them to attacking it.

## Provisional drafting approach

Draft a decision procedure only after precedence is confirmed; the current sentences cannot safely be copied as an algorithm.

This is a research question, not an adopted ruling or a claim that Norbert has answered it. No answer has been supplied yet. Keep the affected rules provisional until Norbert or the council confirms them.

## Sources

Quickstart v0.8, Truthtrance Common Rules Clarifications.

Part of #1831. Record the confirmed answer, its date and a worked example here before closing. Norbert will share this link with the council; this ticket does not send them a message.

comments.body:
Confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> Whichever came first, TT pauses the game, so they can never be at the same time.
> Someone cannot answer something that is in conflict with an existing binding deal, and someone cannot make a new binding deal that is in conflict with a TT answer.

**Rule:** the earlier commitment wins. Truthtrance pauses the game (5 October ruling on #1831), so a Truthtrance answer and a binding deal can never be made at the same moment; one always comes first.

- A Truthtrance answer must not conflict with a binding deal that already exists.
- A new binding deal must not conflict with a Truthtrance answer already given.

**Worked example:** Atreides and Harkonnen have a binding deal that Harkonnen will not attack Arrakeen this turn. Bene Gesserit plays Truthtrance and asks Harkonnen "Will you attack Arrakeen this turn?". Harkonnen must answer "No", because "Yes" would conflict with the existing deal. Reversed: Harkonnen first answers a Truthtrance question with "Yes, I will attack Arrakeen this turn". Afterwards Atreides offers a binding deal that Harkonnen won't attack Arrakeen. Harkonnen cannot make that deal, because it conflicts with the earlier answer.

The Dream Rulebook draft's Truthtrance chapter still needs this added; that is a manuscript edit on #1831, not a remaining question. Closing as answered.
